title: NICHD says answering babble with sounds helps a baby move toward speaking
summary: NICHD's spotlight says responding to a baby's sounds with coos and noises helps the move from babbling toward speaking.
body: The 2017 NICHD spotlight says that babbling with your baby, and responding to their sounds with coos and noises, shows the baby that you hear them and helps them move from babbling to speaking more quickly. The page also says that talking in words, and pausing so the baby can answer, helps the baby learn the flow of conversation. Those are the spotlight's claims about caregiver replies. They are not a measured timetable, and the spotlight does not say a baby who hears fewer replies will fail to speak.

sources.title: Focus on Early Learning

sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Opened 2026-11-26. Supports the sentences about responding to babble with coos and noises, and about pausing so the baby can answer.
